headline: Showers, possibly with a thunderstorm, peak this evening; Tuesday and Wednesday dry out, then a stronger, windier storm arrives Thursday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Showers spread inland this afternoon and become more widespread this evening and overnight, with downpours of up to about a third of an inch per hour. Expect roughly 0.10–0.50 inch along the San Diego County coast and valleys, 0.05–0.20 inch in Orange County, and half an inch to an inch in the mountains. There's a 10% chance of a thunderstorm along the coast until about 10 PM, which could bring sudden gusty winds and brief street flooding. Showers taper off from northwest to southeast Tuesday morning.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Tuesday and Wednesday are mostly dry but stay cool, with highs 2–12 degrees below normal. Wednesday is a few degrees warmer than Tuesday, but only briefly. Mountain and desert winds gust 40–50 mph this evening into Tuesday morning before easing.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thursday brings a weak atmospheric river, a moisture-rich storm with more rain and wind than today's. The chance of more than an inch of rain from early Thursday to early Friday is 20–50% for San Diego County and 70–90% from Orange County north, and an isolated thunderstorm is possible near the coast Thursday afternoon. Mountain and desert gusts reach 40–55 mph, locally 60 mph, and snow levels fall to about 6,500 feet. Rain tapers Friday morning; Friday afternoon and Saturday are dry, with inland highs 7–12 degrees below normal. Another weaker system may arrive Sunday or Monday, but its timing is very uncertain.

coast: High surf continues: 6–8 ft with sets to 10 ft on west-facing beaches this afternoon, and a High Surf Advisory runs until 4 AM Wednesday. Surf drops briefly to 4–6 ft Wednesday, then a new northwest swell Thursday brings dangerous surf and rip currents back into the weekend. Coastal flooding is possible at times with the high surf, and king tides above 7 ft may start around Saturday, November 21. Rough seas for boaters (7–10 ft, gusts 25–30 knots) through Wednesday morning and again Thursday into Friday morning.
watch_for: Brief downpours or a thunderstorm along the coast this evening.
How far north Thursday's storm tracks, which decides how much rain San Diego County gets.
King tides plus big surf this weekend for low-lying beach areas.
confidence: Good confidence in this evening's showers and in Thursday's storm being stronger than today's; rain totals for San Diego County Thursday are still uncertain, and confidence is low for Sunday–Monday.
